points: The upcoming earnings report for the most recently completed quarter will reveal whether Garmin's fitness-watch and subscription momentum carried through the spring/early summer and will set the tone for Q3/back-to-school and Q4/holiday guidance; a strong guide would confirm the long thesis.

The July 2026 TrainingPeaks and TrainHeroic acquisition should start lifting subscription revenue and user attach rates in the current Q3 and into Q4; the upcoming print's guidance and commentary will be the first read on how quickly integration turns a hardware story into a recurring-revenue story.
Aviation revenue gains, a medium-weight driver, could keep growing through Q3 2026 and into 2027, diversifying Garmin away from the direct smartwatch fight with Apple and Samsung.
Apple holds 46% smartwatch share while Garmin is tied with Samsung for second, so the next 12-18 months are about whether Garmin can hold or gain share rather than trying to catch Apple.

The smartwatch market is projected to reach $11.33 billion by 2034 with a 9.36% annual growth rate; Garmin can still outgrow that by expanding subscriptions and premium niches even if total unit growth is modest.
ROKU's Nov. 6 consumer electronics print may offer a holiday-demand read, but Garmin's own Q3 guide and margin trajectory are the real near-term drivers for the long.
